criticChallenges.challenge: {"leadId":"price-gap-federal-vs-oyo","challenge":"Federal contracts include 100-leaf books and distribution to specific constituencies/LGAs (e.g., \"SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION\" titles), while Oyo contracts are procurement-only for 60/80 leaves with massive lot sizes (200k+). Federal lot sizes are 8k–74k, contract years differ (2023–2024 vs 2022 only), and some federal titles specify customization and delivery scope not captured in leaf count alone. These factors constitute legitimate innocent explanations for the observed gap.","disposition":"downgrade"}

{"leadId":"price-gap-federal-vs-oyo","disposition":"downgrade","reason":"The 5.16× price gap on leaf-matched 60/80-leaf books persists after CPI adjustment, but several legitimate cost drivers remain unresolved: (1) Federal contracts explicitly include distribution to dispersed schools across constituencies/LGAs (titles mention \"SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION\" or \"PRINTING AND SUPPLY\"), while Oyo contracts are titled \"procurement\" with no stated delivery scope. (2) Federal lot sizes are 8k–74k vs Oyo's 200k+, giving Oyo massive economies of scale. (3) Federal contracts span 2023–2024 vs Oyo 2022 only; specification upgrades (cover weight, paper GSM, colour, customization level) are not captured in leaf count alone. (4) Geographic dispersion and last-mile delivery to selected schools in specific wards/constituencies add cost. Without detailed spec sheets or a breakdown of production vs distribution, the gap cannot be attributed to overpricing."}

{"leadId":"twin-award-ocds-gyl66f-539001003-002244/17018-ocds-gyl66f-539001003-002381/15613","disposition":"downgrade","reason":"The two federal contracts share the same date (2024-10-15) and quantity (8,200) but target different school clusters (Tudun/S vs Galadimawa II). The near-identical values (0.327% difference) are consistent with separate lots for distinct geographic areas under the same specification, rather than duplicate releases."}

The 5.16× price gap on leaf-matched 60/80-leaf books persists after CPI adjustment, but several legitimate cost drivers remain unresolved: (1) Federal contracts explicitly include distribution to dispersed schools across constituencies/LGAs (titles mention "SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION" or "PRINTING AND SUPPLY"), while Oyo contracts are titled "procurement" with no stated delivery scope. (2) Federal lot sizes are 8k–74k vs Oyo's 200k+, giving Oyo massive economies of scale. (3) Federal contracts span 2023–2024 vs Oyo 2022 only; specification upgrades (cover weight, paper GSM, colour, customization level) are not captured in leaf count alone. (4) Geographic dispersion and last-mile delivery to selected schools in specific wards/constituencies add cost. Without detailed spec sheets or a breakdown of production vs distribution, the gap cannot be attributed to overpricing.

The two awards share the same date (2024-10-15), quantity (8,200), and leaf specification (60/80/100 leaves) but reference different delivery locations ("TUDUN/S" vs "GALADIMAWA II"). This is consistent with separate lots for distinct school clusters or wards within a constituency, each tendered or awarded in parallel. The 0.33% value difference falls within normal rounding or minor spec variance (e.g., cover weight, delivery distance). No evidence suggests duplicate payment.

The 5.16× price gap on matched 60- and 80-leaf books persists after CPI adjustment, but several legitimate factors remain unresolved: federal contracts include explicit distribution to dispersed schools across constituencies/LGAs (titles mention "SUPPLY AND DISTRIBUTION" or "PRINTING AND SUPPLY"), while Oyo contracts appear to be bulk procurement without last-mile delivery; federal lot sizes are 8k–74k versus Oyo's 200k+ per lot, implying significant economies of scale for Oyo; federal contracts span 2021–2024 with varying specifications (some include 20/40/100 leaves, customization levels, cover weight, colour printing not captured by leaf count alone); and geographic spread differs (federal to specific constituencies, Oyo state-wide). Without detailed spec sheets, paper quality, cover GSM, printing colours, and delivery distance breakdowns, the gap cannot be attributed solely to overpricing.
